name: Fontsource
summary: Self-hosted webfonts as npm packages: the same open-source families Google Fonts serves, installed as a build-time dependency with no runtime request to Google.
license: Packages carry each font's own license (mostly OFL); the registry is MIT

steps: Install the family as a package: npm install @fontsource-variable/inter (variable families) or @fontsource/roboto (static families, one package per weight).
Import it once in the JS entry: import "@fontsource-variable/inter". That registers the @font-face and emits the woff2 through your bundler.
Wire the family name into Tailwind v4 with an @theme block: --font-sans: "Inter Variable", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif. Variable family display names take the Variable suffix.

This is exactly how the dashboard layer does it: the two dashboard starters ship their fonts as offline fonts.zip bundles built from @fontsource-variable packages (inter, manrope), with the Google Fonts link tags stripped out.

files.role: One import registers the @font-face rules through the bundler
Point Tailwind v4's font stack at the self-hosted variable families

notes: Choose fontsource over the google-fonts entry whenever the user wants offline-capable builds, GDPR-safe hosting, or version-pinned fonts. The woff2 ships from your own origin, so nothing loads from a third-party CDN at runtime. Family coverage is broad but not every Google family is published; check the registry name before promising one.
